brief.audience_scene: People eating alone after finishing work late
brief.task: A lasting brand line, not a price promotion

facts.source: Fictional demonstration brief; explicit unknown where marked

facts.text: Six single-person stir-fry meals; each ordered portion is individually stir-fried after ordering and served with a bowl of rice. This does not cover every menu item.
facts.source: Fictional demonstration brief; explicit unknown where marked

facts.text: Evening dine-in orders from 20:30 to 23:00. No all-day or delivery-temperature promise.
facts.source: Fictional demonstration brief; explicit unknown where marked

facts.text: The intended audience is people dining alone after a late workday. This is a fictional scenario, not interview evidence.
facts.source: Fictional demonstration brief; explicit unknown where marked

facts.text: The intended attitude: a dinner for one deserves care. No price-promotion theme.
facts.source: Fictional demonstration brief; explicit unknown where marked

facts.text: Long-term brand copy for the menu front and an in-store poster, paired with Late Wok and the category Single-person stir-fried dinners.
facts.source: Fictional demonstration brief; explicit unknown where marked

facts.text: The six dishes make an audible sizzle while cooking and are served hot for dine-in. No measured temperature or service-time claim.
facts.source: Fictional demonstration brief; explicit unknown where marked

facts.text: An unused fictional team draft said Wait for your friends, then start the stir-fry. It is revision material, not a finding about competitors.
facts.source: Fictional demonstration brief; explicit unknown where marked

facts.text: No competitor capability or message research was supplied; uniqueness and existing mental ownership are unknown.
facts.source: Fictional demonstration brief; explicit unknown where marked

candidates.line: Late Wok. A little care in every dinner.

application.principle: A consistent hospitality attitude supported by the actual meal.
application.move: Links the brand to caring about one-person dinner.
application.limit: A proposed brand image, not evidence of established perception.

candidates.tradeoff: Clear attitude; weaker food specificity than C05.

application.principle: A motivating benefit needs supported competitive distinctiveness.
application.move: Connects individual cooking and a specific ordering window.
application.limit: The benefit is supported in the fictional brief, but uniqueness is unresearched.

conditions: USP distinctiveness requires competitor evidence; keep the literal operating window visible.
candidates.tradeoff: Conditional USP application; not eligible for the final three.

candidates.line: You order one. We stir-fry one.

application.principle: Use a concrete supportable preparation detail.
application.move: Connects each order to individual stir-frying.
application.limit: Does not imply never-frozen ingredients; response testing has not occurred.

candidates.tradeoff: Preparation is clear; the late-work occasion is less explicit.

candidates.line: Dinner for one still deserves a wok.

application.principle: A human dining tension carried by an actual product benefit.
application.move: One person is treated as worth cooking a real dinner for.
application.limit: Pair with the restaurant and category; word-image integration is not complete.

candidates.tradeoff: More human warmth than C09, with weaker immediate category identification.

candidates.line: Hear the sizzle. Dinner arrives hot.

application.principle: Find the drama in the product itself.
application.move: Uses actual cooking sound and hot dine-in serving.
application.limit: Dine-in only; no measured temperature, timing or delivery promise.

candidates.tradeoff: Stronger food imagery, weaker brand linkage than C09.

candidates.line: One dish. One bowl of rice. Dinner for one.

application.principle: Lead with a direct and understandable benefit.
application.move: Makes the meal composition and individual portion easy to grasp.
application.limit: No offer or response test is implied.

candidates.tradeoff: Clear meal format, less distinctive phrasing.

candidates.line: Worked late. Still want a freshly stir-fried dinner.

application.principle: Meet an existing desire at the audience awareness level.
application.move: States the meal problem in the supplied intended scenario.
application.limit: An audience assumption in a fictional brief, not a research finding.

candidates.tradeoff: Recognizable situation, but lengthy as a lasting brand line.

candidates.line: Add a stir-fry to the end of your shift.

application.principle: Combine a product detail with a dining occasion.
application.move: Connects adding a dish and ending the workday.
application.limit: Applies recombination, not every stage of a human idea-generation process.

candidates.tradeoff: Useful relationship; needs brand pairing and natural-language testing.

candidates.line: Late Wok. Late shifts, freshly stir-fried dinners.

application.principle: Focus on one intended category and occasion.
application.move: Brand, late work and stir-fried dinner reinforce one position.
application.limit: Proposed focus, not proof of owning the position in customers minds.

candidates.tradeoff: The clearest intended position, though longer in English than Chinese.

candidates.line: A table for one is enough to start the stir-fry.

application.principle: Question a documented convention with relevant difference.
application.move: Reverses the supplied unused draft requiring friends to arrive first.
application.limit: This challenges a specific team draft, not a universal industry norm.

candidates.tradeoff: Inviting but longer and less compact than C04.

recommendations.reason: Clearest brand, category and late-work occasion; less interpretation than C04 and stronger brand linkage than C05.
recommendations.placement: Menu front and in-store poster; keep the full brand and show 20:30–23:00 dine-in ordering hours.
recommendations.condition: Only the six defined evening meals; no all-day, exclusive or delivery-state promise.
recommendations.test: Ask intended diners to recall the brand, food and relevant occasion; compare using the same layout.

recommendations.reason: Gives solo diners a human reason to feel considered; warmer than the lead, less explicit on category.
recommendations.placement: Pair with Late Wok | Single-person stir-fried dinners on the menu or a solo-dining poster.
recommendations.condition: Must actually offer individually cooked single-person meals; do not suggest a private chef.
recommendations.test: Ask what food they expect and whether the line sounds like a restaurant or kitchenware advertisement.

recommendations.reason: Cooking sound and hot serving make the food tangible; more sensory than C04, less brand-specific than the lead.
recommendations.placement: Pair with brand/category and an accurate dine-in food image.
recommendations.condition: Do not use as a delivery-temperature guarantee or add unmeasured timing/temperature.
recommendations.test: Ask what food and sensation come to mind and whether they would look at the menu; stated liking is not an order.

validation.editorial_review: English editorial adaptation of the fictional Chinese example; no native-market consumer test.
